DNS resolution failure for postgres.railway.internal caused it to fail
immediately and report to Sentry (PYTHON-FASTAPI-10). Add
autoretry_for=(OperationalError,) with exponential backoff (max 30s,

transient failures. Split the except block so OperationalError logs a
warning and re-raises for Celery autoretry, while other exceptions still
log the full stacktrace.

Fixes PYTHON-FASTAPI-10

Author: Anurag Duddu
Message:
feat(state): centralize video/project/analysis/transcript state machines with enum enforcement (#24)

* feat(state): add enums + state machines + SQLEnum enforcement

Introduces the app/state/ package with four status enums (VideoStatus,
VideoAnalysisStatus, ProjectStatus, TranscriptStatus), five explicit
transition tables, and five state machine classes (VideoStateMachine,
ProjectStateMachine, VideoAnalysisStateMachine, ProjectAnalysisStateMachine,
TranscriptStateMachine). Every current direct ``row.status = "..."`` write
site will route through one of these in the follow-up refactor commits.

database_models.py switches its four status columns from Column(String(50))
to SQLEnum(..., native_enum=False) — the on-disk type stays VARCHAR so
existing rows and the Alembic chain are untouched, but Python-layer
validation now rejects any value not declared in the enum.

88 new parametrized tests iterate over every (from_state, event, to_state)
tuple in the transition tables so a future edit requires touching both
code and tests — making the Bug B class of regression (HAIC ready-gate
trap, 2026-04-07) impossible to land silently.

Import-order note: app/state/__init__.py exposes the state machines via
PEP 562 __getattr__ lazy loading because database_models.py imports the
status enums from app.state.statuses at module-load time, and eagerly
importing the state machine modules here would recurse back into
database_models and create a cycle.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(state): route project_state_service through ProjectStateMachine

Replaces the bare ``project.status = "..."`` writes in
``update_project_state_for_completion`` with
``ProjectStateMachine.transition`` calls. The Bug B regression guard
(HAIC ready-gate trap, 2026-04-07) now lives in the transition table
as ``(READY, ALL_VIDEOS_COMPLETE) -> COMPLETED``, with a parametrized
test covering it — a future edit cannot silently delete the edge.

Existing test_project_state_service.py coverage continues to pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(state): route watchdog_tasks through the state machines

Switches the watchdog's 4 write branches (stuck VideoAnalysis, stuck
Video-with-analyzing, orphan fix analyzing->analyzed, stuck
ProjectAnalysis, stuck Transcript) to call the appropriate
``*StateMachine.transition`` method. The detection logic (cutoff
timestamps, queries, _ANALYSIS_TIMEOUT / _TRANSCRIPT_TIMEOUT) is
unchanged — only the writes are routed.

The orphan-fix path now fires ``WATCHDOG_CLEANUP`` (analyzing ->
analyzed) which is distinct from ``WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT`` (analyzing ->
error) in the transition table, so the two cleanup intents are
explicit instead of relying on a ``va.status`` branch at the call site.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(state): route pipeline_errors through state machines

``handle_pipeline_error`` and ``handle_project_pipeline_error`` (the
chain ``.on_error`` callbacks) now fire ``CHAIN_FAILED`` at the
appropriate state machine instead of assigning ``row.status = "error"``.

The idempotent self-loop (ERROR, CHAIN_FAILED) -> ERROR in the
transition tables preserves the existing behaviour where the handler
runs harmlessly after a per-step except block already marked the row.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(state): route analysis step tasks through the state machines

Covers the per-video chain (``analysis_steps.py``) and the cross-video
chain (``project_analysis_steps.py``). Every ``row.status = "..."``
write now goes through ``VideoStateMachine``, ``VideoAnalysisStateMachine``,
or ``ProjectAnalysisStateMachine`` — including the terminal
CHAIN_SUCCEEDED from ``analyze_activate_step`` and
``analyze_cross_activate_step``, the CHAIN_STARTED from
``analyze_chunk_step``, and the fail-path in ``_update_analysis_error``
and ``_update_project_analysis_error``.

Preserves the PR #21 retry-reset behaviour: the chunk step's
``VideoAnalysisStateMachine.transition(CHAIN_STARTED)`` call accepts
both PENDING (fresh) and PROCESSING (idempotent re-run after a reset)
as source states.

Preserves the PR #19 error-message preservation behaviour: the state
machine's transition method leaves ``error_message`` unchanged when no
new payload is passed, so the existing pre-stamp pattern in
``_update_analysis_error`` continues to work for the BYOK
insufficient-credits case.

Test-only change: unit tests for the chunk step use MagicMock-based
db/analysis/video fixtures. The MagicMock's auto-generated ``.status``
attribute is not a real string, so ``VideoStatus(row.status)`` raises
``ValueError``. Seed the mock statuses with real strings
("transcribed" / "pending" / "processing" depending on the source
state each test needs).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(state): route transcription_tasks through state machines

Every ``row.status = "..."`` write in ``transcribe_video_task``,
``check_transcription_task``, ``_mark_transcription_error``, and the
PR #22 ``_maybe_auto_dispatch_analyze_chain`` helper now flows through
``VideoStateMachine`` / ``TranscriptStateMachine``.

The auto-dispatch helper uses ``ANALYZE_DISPATCHED`` which clears
``video.error_message`` as a side effect (identical behaviour to the
explicit assign it replaces).

The transition table's ``(UPLOADED, TRANSCRIBE_FAILED) -> ERROR``
edge covers the early-failure path in ``transcribe_video_task``'s
outer except block, which can fire before the worker has promoted
the row to TRANSCRIBING (e.g., an R2 download error). Similarly
``(PENDING, TRANSCRIBE_FAILED) -> ERROR`` covers the transcript side.

Test-only change: same MagicMock status-seeding as the
analysis_steps commit — the transcription task fetches the Video and
Transcript from the DB and passes them to the state machine, which
needs real strings.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(state): route routes/videos.py through the state machines

Every direct ``video.status = "..."`` / ``transcript.status = "..."``
/ ``analysis.status = "..."`` write in ``routes/videos.py`` now goes
through the appropriate state machine:

- ``/upload-url``: ``UPLOAD_URL_REQUESTED`` (None -> UPLOADING)
- ``/upload`` (legacy): chains ``UPLOAD_URL_REQUESTED`` +
  ``UPLOAD_CONFIRMED`` so the state machine sees both edges
- ``/confirm-upload``: ``UPLOAD_CONFIRMED`` — the transition table
  covers all three legal source states (UPLOADING, UPLOADED, ERROR)
  so the PR #20 false-negative recovery path is preserved
- ``/transcribe``: ``TRANSCRIBE_REQUESTED`` on the video +
  ``ROW_CREATED`` on the transcript (which handles new rows and
  existing ERROR / PENDING / PROCESSING rows via the transition table)
- ``/analyze``: ``ANALYZE_DISPATCHED`` on the video + the PR #21
  retry-reset block re-expressed as
  ``VideoAnalysisStateMachine.transition(RETRY_RESET)``. The JSONB
  payload clears stay as before — they are not state-machine concerns
- 5x per-step routes: ``ANALYZE_DISPATCHED`` (self-loop from ANALYZING
  between steps is idempotent by design in the transition table)

The concurrency guard check (``video.status == "analyzing"``) and the
PR #20 ``status=="uploading"`` 409 guard in ``/transcribe`` are
untouched — they read status, they don't write it.

The strict ``/transcribe`` guard from PR #20 (reject uploads still in
"uploading") is preserved, as is the PR #20 ``/confirm-upload``
idempotency. The PR #21 retry-reset block is preserved verbatim
except for the status write.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore(alembic): record schema version bump for SQLEnum enforcement

PR #22 switched four status columns from ``Column(String(50))`` to
``Column(SQLEnum(..., native_enum=False, ...))``. Because
``native_enum=False`` keeps the on-disk type as ``VARCHAR(50)``, no
DDL change is required — but we bump the Alembic head here so
teammates pulling main after the PR see the schema version advance
and know the enum enforcement landed at this point.

A future migration to native Postgres ENUM types (PR #22 scope
explicitly excludes this) would be the heavy-lifting migration.

Author: Anurag Duddu
Message:
fix(state): allow ready->completed transition (project state-machine trap) (#17)

ProjectStateService.update_project_state_for_completion gates the
"completed" transition on project.status being in ("planning",
"processing"). But the same method TRANSITIONS the project to "ready"
the moment any video reaches "transcribed". So:

  planning -> ready    (first transcript done)
  planning/processing  -> completed (all videos done)

Once a project enters "ready" it can never advance to "completed",
because the gate excludes "ready". This is a one-way trap.

Production evidence: the HAIC project (id 8b894631-2d32-4593-ae2a-
e76e6d9f84f3) is currently stuck at status="ready" with 5/6 videos at
video_analyses.status="completed". The frontend then polls
/api/projects/{id}/analysis (because status="ready" implies the
analysis tab should work), gets a 404, and renders a broken page.

Fix: add "ready" to the gate tuple. Surgical, single-line behavioral
change. The "ready" -> "completed" transition is also the only path the
LAST-video activate step can use in practice, since by then the project
has long since left "planning".

Tests: new tests/test_project_state_service.py covers the regression
(test_ready_to_completed_transition) plus three guardrails to prove the
existing planning->completed, planning->ready, and partial-completion
behaviours still hold. Verified red->green: the new test fails on the
old code with `'ready' == 'completed'`, passes after the fix. Full
project-state suite (12 tests across this file + test_watchdog_race.py)
passes. Ruff clean.

Message:
fix: coerce bare-string EXPLAIN insights into dict shape

Llama-4-Scout (default standard model) occasionally returns the EXPLAIN
response as a list of bare headline strings instead of a list of insight
objects. The output validator rejects items that aren't dicts; the
existing one-shot retry produced the same shape; the pipeline halted
after burning ~2 minutes on chunk/infer/relate. Caught in production at
21:11 UTC for video ceb5bdaf — first user to successfully advance past
chunk after the deadlock fix landed, then hit this immediately.

Fix:
- Add _coerce_insight_items() in explain.py that wraps any bare-string
  item into a minimal valid insight dict ({headline, explanation,
  confidence: medium, type: non-consensus, ...}). Empty strings are
  dropped. Non-list inputs pass through unchanged so the validator can
  still produce its normal error.
- Run coercion immediately after both LLM calls (initial + retry) so
  validation operates on coerced data.
- Augment EXPLAIN_SYSTEM_PROMPT with an explicit WRONG/RIGHT example
  contrasting bare strings against the full object shape, as defense.

The codebase owner explicitly said standard-key (shared Methodex)
users must not hit format failures — this is part of that.

9 new tests in test_explain_coercion.py cover:
- well-formed dicts pass through
- bare strings coerced
- mixed list coerced
- empty strings dropped
- empty list still rejected
- integration tests via explain_node with mocked llm_service

400 tests total (was 391), ruff clean.

Out of scope but flagged: same coercion pattern likely needed for the
other 4 nodes (infer, relate, activate) and the 3 cross-video nodes.
Defense-in-depth follow-up.

after burning ~2 minutes on chunk/infer/relate. Caught in production at
21:11 UTC for video ceb5bdaf — first user to successfully advance past
chunk after the deadlock fix landed, then hit this immediately.

- Add _coerce_insight_items() in explain.py that wraps any bare-string
  item into a minimal valid insight dict ({headline, explanation,
  confidence: medium, type: non-consensus, ...}). Empty strings are
  dropped. Non-list inputs pass through unchanged so the validator can
  still produce its normal error.
- Run coercion immediately after both LLM calls (initial + retry) so
  validation operates on coerced data.
- Augment EXPLAIN_SYSTEM_PROMPT with an explicit WRONG/RIGHT example
  contrasting bare strings against the full object shape, as defense.

users must not hit format failures — this is part of that.

- well-formed dicts pass through
- bare strings coerced
- mixed list coerced
- empty strings dropped
- empty list still rejected
- integration tests via explain_node with mocked llm_service

other 4 nodes (infer, relate, activate) and the 3 cross-video nodes.
